proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(q_a=\Pi_{s_a}\), \(D_a=D_{s_a}\), and \(\overline D=\sum_aq_aD_a=M(\Pi)\).  For matrices \(X_a\) of a common dimension and \(\overline X=\sum_aq_aX_a\), direct expansion using \(\sum_aq_a=1\) gives
\[
 \sum_aq_a(X_a-\overline X)^{\top}J(X_a-\overline X)
 =\frac12\sum_{a,b}q_aq_b(X_a-X_b)^{\top}J(X_a-X_b).
\]
Indeed, each side equals
\[
 \sum_aq_aX_a^{\top}JX_a-\overline X^{\top}J\overline X.
\]
Taking \(X_a=D_a\), deleting the terms with \(a=b\), pairing \((a,b)\) with \((b,a)\), and applying the definitions of \(G\), \(E_{ab}\), and \(B_{ab}\), we obtain
\[
 G(\Pi)=\frac1T\sum_{a<b}q_aq_bE_{ab}^{\top}JE_{ab}
 =\sum_{a<b}q_aq_bB_{ab}.
\]

Fix \((t,\ell)\), set \(x_a=(D_a)_{t,\ell}\), and expand similarly:
\[
 \sum_aq_a(D_a-\overline D)^{\top}Je_tx_a
 =\sum_{a<b}q_aq_b(D_a-D_b)^{\top}Je_t(x_a-x_b).
\]
Both sides equal
\[
 \sum_aq_aD_a^{\top}Je_tx_a-\overline D^{\top}Je_t\sum_aq_ax_a.
\]
Since \(R_{s_a}=J(D_a-\overline D)\), \(x_a-x_b=(E_{ab})_{t,\ell}\), and \(J\) is symmetric, division by \(T\) yields
\[
 h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)=\sum_{a<b}q_aq_bb_{ab,t,\ell}.
\]

The matrix \(J=I_T-\mathbf 1_T\mathbf 1_T^{\top}/T\) is symmetric and idempotent.  Therefore, for every \(v\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 v^{\top}B_{ab}v=T^{-1}(E_{ab}v)^{\top}J(E_{ab}v)
 =T^{-1}\lVert JE_{ab}v\rVert_2^2.
\]
The reshaping floor implies \(q_aq_b\geq\epsilon^2>0\).  Hence the pair formula gives
\[
 v^{\top}G(\Pi)v=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 JE_{ab}v=0\quad\hbox{for every }a<b.
\]
Likewise,
\[
 v^{\top}H_{\mathcal S}v
 =T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}\lVert JE_{ab}v\rVert_2^2.
\]
Thus
\[
 \ker G(\Pi)=\bigcap_{a<b}\ker(JE_{ab})=\ker H_{\mathcal S}.
\]
No step used absorption or the numerical values of the positive masses.  The common kernel depends only on the listed support, proving that nonsingularity for one positive law is equivalent to nonsingularity for every positive law on \(\mathcal S\).

Path overlap gives \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}>0\), so all ratios in \(\theta(\Pi)\) are defined.  Conditional on \(X\), consistency and pathwise conditional mean random assignment imply, componentwise,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left.\frac{\Pi_W}{\pi_W(X)}A_W(\Pi)Y\right|X\right]
 &=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\pi_s(X)\frac{\Pi_s}{\pi_s(X)}A_s(\Pi)
       \mathbb E_P[Y\mid W=s,X]\\
 &=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)\mu(s,X).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let \(m(X)=(m_1(X),\ldots,m_T(X))^{\top}\).  The calendar-memory assumption is the vector identity
\[
 \mu(s,X)=m(X)+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}
 e_t\tau_{t,\ell}(X)(D_s)_{t,\ell}.
\]
Because \(M(\Pi)=\sum_s\Pi_sD_s\),
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)
 =J\left\{\sum_s\Pi_sD_s-M(\Pi)\sum_s\Pi_s\right\}=0.
\]
Consequently the unrestricted baseline cancels:
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)m(X)
 =T^{-1}G(\Pi)^{-1}\left\{\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}\right\}m(X)=0.
\]
For each effect cell,
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)e_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}
 =G(\Pi)^{-1}\left\{T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}e_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}\right\}
 =L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi).
\]
Taking expectation over \(X\), using the finite sums and \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\mathbb E_P[\tau_{t,\ell}(X)]\), proves
\[
 \theta(\Pi)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{t,\ell}.
\]
The inverse exists by residual full rank.

For the design identities, regard \(s\) as a random path with law \(\Pi\).  Since \((D_s)_{t,j}=s_{t-j}\), the \((j,r)\) entry of \(G\) is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_{jr}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}J_{tv}
   \operatorname{Cov}_{\Pi}(s_{t-j},s_{v-r})\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
 -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(J_{tv}=\mathbf 1\{t=v\}-T^{-1}\).  Similarly,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}J_{vt}\operatorname{Cov}_{\Pi}(s_{v-j},s_{t-\ell})\\
 &=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
 -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
These calculations use only a finite binary support.  If every path is absorbing, then \(s_u=\mathbf 1\{a(s)\leq u\}\), with the boundary value zero.  Therefore
\[
 C_{\Pi}(u,v)=F_{\Pi}(\min\{u,v\})-F_{\Pi}(u)F_{\Pi}(v)=K_{\Pi}(u,v),
\]
which proves the ordered-Green corollary.

Finally, with \(e_{\ell}\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}D_se_{\ell}\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}\{D_s-M(\Pi)\}e_{\ell}\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}R_s(\Pi)e_{\ell}
 =G(\Pi)e_{\ell}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The second equality uses \(\sum_s\Pi_sR_s=0\), and the third uses symmetry and idempotence of \(J\).  Multiplication by \(G(\Pi)^{-1}\) yields
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=e_j^{\top}e_{\ell}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\]

Under calendar homogeneity, write the common effect at lag \(\ell\) as \(\overline\tau_{\ell}\).  The calendar-loading theorem and its normalization give
\[
 \theta_j(\Pi)
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{\ell}
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\overline\tau_{\ell}
 =\overline\tau_j.
\]
This proves the first assertion inside the present model class.  The separate published-class theorem proves the corresponding estimator limit under Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo's actual design conditions, so no inclusion relation between the two sampling classes is used.

For the witness, in the order \((000,001,011)\),
\[
 D_{000}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 D_{001}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 D_{011}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 M=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1/3&0\\2/3&1/3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since
\[
 J=\begin{pmatrix}2/3&-1/3&-1/3\\-1/3&2/3&-1/3\\-1/3&-1/3&2/3\end{pmatrix},
\]
direct substitution into \(R_s=J(D_s-M)\), \(G=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s^{\top}R_s\), and the definition of \(h\) gives
\[
 G=\begin{pmatrix}2/27&0\\0&4/81\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
 h_{2,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/27\\-2/81\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 h_{3,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/27\\2/81\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 h_{3,1}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\4/81\end{pmatrix},
\]
with every other numerator zero.  Multiplication by \(G^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(27/2,81/4)\) yields
\[
 L_{\cdot,2,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/2\\-1/2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 L_{\cdot,3,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/2\\1/2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 L_{\cdot,3,1}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The asserted formulas for \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_1\) follow from the causal loading representation.  In particular, \(\theta_1\) varies with two calendar-specific current effects even when \(\tau_{3,1}\) is fixed.

To embed the witness in the published design, independently draw every \(W_i\) from \(\Pi\), let the supported potential outcomes be deterministic and bounded with
\[
 Y_{it}(w)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{1}\tau_{t,\ell}w_{t-\ell},
\]
and use the known propensity \(\pi_i(s)=1/3\) on the three paths.  Then \(\rho_{ij}=0\) for \(i\neq j\), \(\rho_{ii}=1\), and hence \(n^{-2}\sum_{i,j}\rho_{ij}=1/n\); overlap holds with \(c_{*}=1/3\), and the finite collection of deterministic outcomes has a uniform second-moment bound.  The displayed positive-definite \(G\) supplies rank.  Thus the same nonreduction occurs within the published sampling setup once calendar-varying effects are admitted.

Every listed \(D_s\) and \(E_{ab}\) is integral, while \(J=I_T-\mathbf 1_T\mathbf 1_T^{\top}/T\) is rational.  Hence \(B_{ab}\), \(b_{ab,t,\ell}\), and \(H_{\mathcal S}\) are obtained by finitely many exact rational operations.

Apply Gaussian elimination over \(\mathbb Q\) to the \(d\)-dimensional matrix \(H_{\mathcal S}\).  If it is singular, elimination returns a nonzero \(v\in\mathbb Q^d\) with \(H_{\mathcal S}v=0\).  The support-rank sum of squares then gives
\[
 0=v^{\top}H_{\mathcal S}v
 =T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}\lVert JE_{ab}v\rVert_2^2,
\]
so \(JE_{ab}v=0\) for every pair.  This is the claimed exact singularity certificate.

If \(H_{\mathcal S}\) is nonsingular, the support-rank lemma and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon>0\) imply that \(G(\Pi)\) is nonsingular.  Rationality of \(\Pi\) and the pair identities imply that every entry of \(G\) and each \(h_{t,\ell}\) is rational.  Exact elimination therefore computes \(G^{-1}\) and every entry of
\[
 L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)=G(\Pi)^{-1}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi).
\]
The rational weights \(\omega_{\ell,t}\) make \(Q\) rational.  There are finitely many cells \((j,t,\ell)\); exact comparison of each rational number \(L_{j,t,\ell}-Q_{j,t,\ell}\) with zero returns its sign, including equality, and summing the exact absolute values returns \(\mathcal C(\Pi,Q)\).  Both branches terminate because all matrices and index sets are finite.

An absorbing binary path is determined by its adoption date: if \(u=a(s)\), then \(s_r=\mathbf 1\{u\leq r\}\), with \(u=T+1\) for the never-treated path.  Distinct absorbing paths therefore have distinct adoption dates.  For \(a<b\), the boundary convention gives
\[
 (E_{ab})_{r,j}
 =\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq r-j\}-\mathbf 1\{u_b\leq r-j\}
 =\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq r-j<u_b\}
 =(I_{ab})_{r,j}.
\]
Thus \(E_{ab}=I_{ab}\), including all shifted boundary cases.  The absorbing graph-rank lemma proves the stated equivalence between \(\ker H_{\mathcal S}=\{0\}\) and connectivity of every lag vertex to \(\bot\).

Positivity makes every adjacent ratio well defined.  Recursion and \(\sum_a\Pi_{s_a}=1\) give
\[
 \frac{\Pi_{s_a}}{\Pi_{s_1}}=\prod_{r=1}^{a-1}\rho_r=z_a,
 \qquad
 \Pi_{s_a}=\frac{z_a}{Z}.
\]
Substitution into the pair-mass identities yields
\[
 G(\Pi)=Z^{-2}\Gamma(\rho),
 \qquad
 h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)=Z^{-2}g_{t,\ell}(\rho).
\]
The support-rank premise and positive masses imply \(G(\Pi)\succ0\), so \(\Gamma(\rho)=Z^2G(\Pi)\succ0\) and \(\det\Gamma(\rho)>0\).  The common scale cancels:
\[
 L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\Gamma(\rho)^{-1}g_{t,\ell}(\rho).
\]

Let \(\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma)\) be the cofactor adjugate.  Expansion by a column proves \(\Gamma\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma)=\det(\Gamma)I_d\): diagonal entries are the determinant expansion, while off-diagonal entries are determinants of matrices with two equal columns and therefore vanish by cancellation of paired permutations.  The same expansion after replacing column \(j\) by \(g_{t,\ell}\) gives
\[
 e_j^{\top}\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma)g_{t,\ell}=\Delta_{j,t,\ell}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)
 =\frac{\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)}{\det\Gamma(\rho)}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive, proving the sign and zero equivalences, and their finite conjunction proves the off-diagonal assertion.

Finally, \(\Pi_{s_a}=z_a/Z\) makes the floor equivalent to \(z_a\geq\epsilon Z\).  Each \(z_a\) is a monomial in the adjacent ratios, and the endpoint matrices have integer entries.  Hence \(\Gamma\), \(g\), and \(\Delta\) are finite polynomials with rational coefficients in rationally represented ratios.  Exact determinant evaluation and sign comparison therefore terminate.  This argument evaluates one supplied ratio vector; it makes no assertion that the connected components of the complements of the determinant zero sets have been globally enumerated.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose every path in \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing and \(\Pi_s>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\).  Then
\[
 \dim\ker G(\Pi)
 =\#\{\text{connected components of }\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S,p}\text{ not containing }\bot\}.
\]
In particular, \(G(\Pi)\) is positive definite if and only if every vertex \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) is connected to \(\bot\).  The equality need not hold for a law on the boundary of the simplex.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Order the absorbing paths by increasing adoption date.  For a pair with dates \(u_a<u_b\), put \(x=E_{ab}v\) and extend the coordinates of \(v\) by \(v_j=0\) for \(j\notin\{0,\ldots,p\}\).  The interval representation of \(E_{ab}\) gives
\[
 x_t=\sum_{j=0}^{p}v_j\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq t-j<u_b\}.
\]
Taking the difference of consecutive rows, for every \(t\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), yields
\[
 x_t-x_{t-1}=v_{t-u_a}-v_{t-u_b}.
\]
Because \(Jx=0\) if and only if \(x\) is constant, we have
\[
 JE_{ab}v=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 v_{t-u_a}=v_{t-u_b}\quad\text{for every }t\in\{2,\ldots,T\}.
\]
If both indices are in \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\), this is precisely equality across the corresponding graph edge.  If exactly one is in range, the other coordinate is zero and the equation is equality with the value at \(\bot\), which is fixed to zero.  If neither is in range, the equation is \(0=0\) and adds no restriction.

The support-rank lemma is applicable because every mass is positive, and therefore identifies \(\ker G(\Pi)\) with the intersection of these pairwise constraints.  A vector in that intersection is constant on every connected component of \(\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S,p}\), and its constant is zero on the component containing \(\bot\).  Conversely, assigning an arbitrary constant to each other component and zero to the component of \(\bot\) satisfies every edge equation.  These component indicators are linearly independent and span the kernel, proving the dimension formula and the positive-definiteness criterion.

Positivity is essential.  Take \(T=2\), \(p=0\), \(\mathcal S=\{00,01\}\), and the boundary law \(\Pi_{00}=1\), \(\Pi_{01}=0\).  At \(t=2\), the two adoption dates produce an edge joining lag vertex \(0\) to \(\bot\), so the graph has no component away from \(\bot\).  But \(D_W=D_{00}=0\) almost surely under this boundary law, whence \(G(\Pi)=0\) and \(\dim\ker G(\Pi)=1\).  This is the asserted boundary counterexample.
added_lemmas.justification: The component formula turns support rank for absorbing paths into a finite graph-connectivity test and explicitly records the positivity condition needed for the equality.
added_lemmas.gap: The ordered pair-mass kernel alone gives a matrix test; it does not expose the exact combinatorial dimension of the unidentified lag subspace.
added_lemmas.consumer: The public \(\texttt{ripw}\) workflow can explain a failed rank check by listing lag vertices disconnected from the boundary vertex.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the published-class setup of the distributed-lag RIPW estimator, suppose its three stated regularity conditions hold, the unit-specific generalized propensities are known, \(G(\Pi)\succ0\), and
\[
 \mathbb E[Y_{it}(w)]=\mu_{it}+\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\tau_{i,t,\ell}w_{t-\ell}
\]
for every \(i\), \(t\), and \(w\), with \(w_u=0\) outside \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\).  Put \(\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\tau_{i,t,\ell}\).  Then
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}-
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}
 =o_P(1).
\]
If \(\tau_{i,t,\ell}=\tau_{i,-\ell}\) for every legal \(t\), then, for each \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\),
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}_{-\ell}
 =n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\tau_{i,-\ell}+o_P(1),
\]
which is exactly the conclusion of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo's Theorem \(4.1\) under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup and Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(r_i=r_i(W_i)\).  The support overlap and \(0\leq\Pi_s\leq1\) imply \(0\leq r_i\leq c_*^{-1}\).  If \(U_i\) is any scalar entry of \(r_i\), \(r_iD_{W_i}\), \(r_iD_{W_i}^{\top}JD_{W_i}\), or \(r_iD_{W_i}^{\top}JY_i\), then the bounded design, fixed \(T\), and the uniform second-moment condition give \(\sup_i\mathbb E[U_i^2]<\infty\).  By the definition of maximal correlation,
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(U_i,U_j)|
 \leq \rho_{ij}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(U_i)\operatorname{Var}(U_j)}
 \leq C\rho_{ij}
\]
for a finite constant \(C\) independent of \(i,j,n\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(U_i-\mathbb E U_i)\right)
 \leq Cn^{-2}\sum_{i,j}\rho_{ij}=O(n^{-q}).
\]
For every \(\delta>0\), applying the elementary inequality \(\mathbf 1\{|Z|>\delta\}\leq Z^2/\delta^2\) and taking expectations shows that each such sample average differs from its expectation by \(o_P(1)\).  There are only finitely many matrix entries because \(T\) and \(p\) are fixed.

Conditional assignment on the full potential-outcome schedule gives, for every supported \(s\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[r_i\mathbf 1\{W_i=s\}f(\mathscr Y_i)\right]
 =\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\Pi_s}{\pi_i(s)}pi_i(s)f(\mathscr Y_i)\right]
 =\Pi_s\mathbb E[f(\mathscr Y_i)].
\]
Taking \(f=1\) and design coordinates yields
\[
 n^{-1}\sum_i r_i=1+o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \overline D_n:=\frac{\sum_i r_iD_{W_i}}{\sum_i r_i}=M(\Pi)+o_P(1).
\]

The grand intercept and the restrictions \(\sum_i\alpha_i=0\), \(\sum_t\lambda_t=0\) parameterize all unit constants and all common time contrasts.  Eliminating them from the weighted least-squares problem first applies \(J\) within each unit and then subtracts the weighted cross-unit mean.  Thus, on the event that its normal matrix is nonsingular, the coefficient obeys
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}=\widehat G_n^{-1}\widehat g_n,
\]
where
\[
 \widehat G_n=\frac1{nT}\sum_i r_i(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n)^{\top}J(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n),
\]
\[
 \widehat g_n=\frac1{nT}\sum_i r_i(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n)^{\top}JY_i.
\]
The outcome weighted mean drops from the second normal equation because \(\sum_i r_i(D_{W_i}-\overline D_n)=0\).  This exact elimination also shows why the grand intercept cannot be omitted when both fixed-effect sums are constrained.

The preceding finite-dimensional laws of large numbers and \(\overline D_n=M+o_P(1)\) give
\[
 \widehat G_n
 =\frac1T\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J(D_s-M)+o_P(1)
 =G(\Pi)+o_P(1).
\]
For the numerator, replacing \(\overline D_n\) by \(M\) costs \(o_P(1)\): the replacement error is the product of \(\overline D_n-M=o_P(1)\) and a weighted outcome average that is \(O_P(1)\) by the same second-moment calculation.  Conditional assignment and the calendar-varying mean model then imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1T r_i(D_{W_i}-M)^{\top}JY_i\right]
 &=\frac1T\sum_s\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J
 \left\{\mu_i+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}e_t\tau_{i,t,\ell}(D_s)_{t,\ell}\right\}\\
 &=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{i,t,\ell}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mu_i=(\mu_{i1},\ldots,\mu_{iT})^{\top}\), and its contribution is zero because \(\sum_s\Pi_s(D_s-M)=0\).  Averaging over \(i\) and applying the variance bound yields
\[
 \widehat g_n
 =\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}+o_P(1).
\]
Since \(G(\Pi)\succ0\), its smallest eigenvalue is positive.  Entrywise convergence in the fixed dimension implies that \(\widehat G_n\) is nonsingular with probability tending to one and \(\widehat G_n^{-1}=G(\Pi)^{-1}+o_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}
 =\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}G(\Pi)^{-1}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}+o_P(1),
\]
which is the first conclusion.  Under calendar homogeneity, the normalization \(\sum_tL_{j,t,\ell}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\) reduces its \(j\)-th coordinate to \(n^{-1}\sum_i\tau_{i,-j}+o_P(1)\), proving the second conclusion under exactly the published design layer.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the anchor-faithful estimator result: it retains the published grand intercept, unit-specific known propensities, and weakly dependent triangular-array sampling while allowing calendar-varying lag effects.
added_lemmas.gap: The published theorem proves only calendar-homogeneous dynamic recovery and explicitly leaves the time-varying DATE equation outside its scope.
added_lemmas.consumer: Applied users obtain the same loading tensor as an actual probability limit in the published design-based regime, with exact homogeneous recovery as a corollary.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every law in \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)\), with \(\mathcal S\) any finite binary-path support, the reshaped fixed-effect coefficient satisfies
\[
 \theta(\Pi)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{t,\ell}.
\]
For \(j,r,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), the arbitrary-path covariance kernel obeys
\[
 G_{jr}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
 -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r),
\]
\[
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
 -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\},
\]
and \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\).  If every path in \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, then \(C_{\Pi}=K_{\Pi}\), so the same two formulas hold with \(K_{\Pi}\) in place of \(C_{\Pi}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After enlarging the base support to arbitrary binary paths, the adoption-time Green kernel is not the general covariance kernel.  The corrected claim uses \(C_{\Pi}\) generally and recovers \(K_{\Pi}\) only under absorption.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
If \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\tau_{r,\ell}\) for every \(t,r\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), then \(\theta_j(\Pi)=\tau_{t,j}\) for every \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) and every legal \(t\).  For \(T=3\), \(p=1\), \(\mathcal S=\{000,001,011\}\), and \(\Pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), the calendar-varying model yields
\[
 \theta_0=(\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2,
 \qquad
 \theta_1=(-\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2+\tau_{3,1}.
\]
Thus the coefficient vector is not determined by a time-homogeneous lag-effect vector.  The first equality is coefficient algebra in the present superpopulation class, not a class-inclusion proof of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo's Theorem \(4.1\).  The published-class calendar-loading theorem supplies the faithful statistical recovery of that theorem, and the displayed witness admits an independent randomized-assignment embedding satisfying its hypotheses.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current statement falsely claims class inclusion with the published theorem.  The corrected claim separates superpopulation coefficient algebra from the new anchor-faithful estimator corollary and retains the explicit strictness witness.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose every path in \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing.  Order the distinct paths as \(\mathcal S=(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\), put \(u_a=a(s_a)\), and require \(u_a<u_b\) for \(a<b\).  Suppose \(\ker H_{\mathcal S}=\{0\}\), equivalently every lag vertex of \(\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S,p}\) is connected to \(\bot\).  For a fixed law with \(\Pi_{s_a}\geq\epsilon>0\), define \(\rho_a=\Pi_{s_{a+1}}/\Pi_{s_a}\), \(z_1=1\), \(z_a=\prod_{r=1}^{a-1}\rho_r\), and \(Z=\sum_{a=1}^{k}z_a\).  Define \(I_{ab}\in\{0,1\}^{T\times d}\) by \((I_{ab})_{r,j}=\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq r-j<u_b\}\), and set
\[
 \Gamma(\rho)=T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}z_az_bI_{ab}^{\top}JI_{ab},
 \qquad
 g_{t,\ell}(\rho)=T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}z_az_bI_{ab}^{\top}Je_t(I_{ab})_{t,\ell}.
\]
Then \(\det\Gamma(\rho)>0\).  If \(\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)\) is the determinant obtained by replacing column \(j\) of \(\Gamma(\rho)\) by \(g_{t,\ell}(\rho)\), then for every \(j,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) and \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\),
\[
 L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\frac{\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)}{\det\Gamma(\rho)},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sgn}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\operatorname{sgn}\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho),
\]
and \(L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=0\) if and only if \(\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)=0\).  Hence all off-diagonal causal-lag loadings vanish at this law if and only if these determinants vanish for every \(t\) and every \(j\neq\ell\).  The floor is equivalent to \(z_a\geq\epsilon Z\) for every \(a\).  For rational endpoints and ratios, all displayed quantities and signs are computable by terminating exact rational arithmetic, including shifted boundary coordinates.  This is a pointwise certificate for a supplied law; it does not classify the global sign chambers over all admissible ratios.

proposed.name: Calendar-varying finite-memory RIPW class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)\) is the set of tuples \((P,\Pi,\mu,m,\tau)\) such that \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{0,1\}^{T}\) is finite and nonempty, \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\) almost surely for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), consistency and pathwise conditional mean random assignment hold, \(\mu_t(s,X)=m_t(X)+\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\tau_{t,\ell}(X)(D_s)_{t,\ell}\) for every \(s\) and \(t\), and \(G(\Pi)\succ0\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The causal superpopulation class should use the enlarged arbitrary binary-path support while remaining distinct from the published unit-indexed sampling layer.

proposed.name: Arbitrary-path covariance kernel
proposed.construction:
Extend every \(s\in\mathcal S\) by \(s_u=0\) for \(u\notin\{1,\ldots,T\}\), put \(\overline s_u=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s s_u\), and define
\[
 C_{\Pi}(u,v)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s(s_u-\overline s_u)(s_v-\overline s_v),
 \qquad (u,v)\in\mathbb Z^2.
\]
Thus \(C_{\Pi}\) is the coordinate covariance kernel under the finite law \(s\sim\Pi\), without an absorbing-path restriction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition supplies the correct covariance coordinate for arbitrary binary-path algebra.

proposed.name: Absorbing ordered Green kernel
proposed.construction: When every path in \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, order the paths by \(a(s)\), define \(F_{\Pi}(u)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s\mathbf 1\{a(s)\leq u\}\), and set \(K_{\Pi}(u,v)=F_{\Pi}(\min\{u,v\})-F_{\Pi}(u)F_{\Pi}(v)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The bridge-kernel representation is valid only for absorbing paths and is now stated as that corollary of the arbitrary covariance kernel.

proposed.name: Path-pair contributions
proposed.construction: Fix any enumeration \(\mathcal S=(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\).  For \(1\leq a<b\leq k\), \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), set \(E_{ab}=D_{s_a}-D_{s_b}\), \(B_{ab}=T^{-1}E_{ab}^{\top}JE_{ab}\), \(b_{ab,t,\ell}=T^{-1}E_{ab}^{\top}Je_t(E_{ab})_{t,\ell}\), and \(H_{\mathcal S}=\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq k}B_{ab}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The pair-mass identities are enumeration invariant and apply before imposing absorbing order.

proposed.name: Absorbing-support lag graph
proposed.construction: Suppose every path in \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing.  The graph \(\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S,p}\) has vertex set \(\{\bot,0,\ldots,p\}\).  For every unordered pair of distinct adoption dates \(u_a=a(s_a)\), \(u_b=a(s_b)\), and every \(t\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), put \(r=t-u_a\) and \(q=t-u_b\).  If \(r,q\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), add the edge \(\{r,q\}\); if exactly one of \(r,q\) belongs to \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\), join that vertex to \(\bot\); and otherwise add no edge.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This graph records exactly the first-difference equalities generated by an absorbing support.

proposed.name: Published-class distributed-lag RIPW estimator
proposed.construction:
For each \(n\), let \(\{(\mathscr Y_i,W_i):i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\}\) be a possibly dependent triangular array, where \(W_i\in\{0,1\}^{T}\), \(\mathscr Y_i=\{Y_{it}(w):t\in\{1,\ldots,T\},\ w\in\{0,1\}^{T}\}\), and \(Y_{it}=Y_{it}(W_i)\).  Define the known unit-specific generalized propensity
\[
 \pi_i(w)=\mathbb P_n(W_i=w\mid\mathscr Y_i)
\]
and let \(\rho_{ij}\) be the maximal correlation between measurable square-integrable functions of \((\mathscr Y_i,W_i)\) and \((\mathscr Y_j,W_j)\).  The published regularity conditions are: for some \(q\in(0,1]\),
\[
 n^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\rho_{ij}=O(n^{-q});
\]
for some \(c_{*}>0\), \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_{*}\) for every \(i\) and every \(s\in\mathcal S\); and for some \(M_{2}<\infty\),
\[
 \max_{i,t,w}\mathbb E[Y_{it}(w)^2]\leq M_{2}.
\]
For a reshaping law \(\Pi\) supported on \(\mathcal S\), define
\[
 r_i(w)=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_w/\pi_i(w),&w\in\mathcal S,\\
 0,&w\notin\mathcal S.
 \end{cases}
\]
The published-class distributed-lag RIPW estimator, with the grand intercept retained, is any coefficient vector \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}=(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}_{0},\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}_{-1},\ldots,\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{ex}}_{-p})^{\top}\) solving
\[
 \min_{\substack{\beta\in\mathbb R^{d},\ \mu_0\in\mathbb R,\
                   \alpha\in\mathbb R^n,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R^T\\
                   \sum_i\alpha_i=0,\ \sum_t\lambda_t=0}}
 \sum_{i=1}^{n}r_i(W_i)
 \left\|Y_i-\mu_0\mathbf 1_T-\alpha_i\mathbf 1_T-\lambda-D_{W_i}\beta\right\|_2^2.
\]
These are Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo's known-propensity design and Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\), specialized only by taking the reshaping support to be \(\mathcal S\), and their equation \((4.2)\) with \(D_{W_i}\) collecting the current treatment and its \(p\) lags.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The published sampling layer and its corrected equation (4.2) estimator must be formalized separately from the i.i.d. superpopulation identification class; the grand intercept and the off-support zero weight are explicit.
Its promised adjacent-mass \(LDL^{\top}\) and Cauchy--Binet chamber analysis was not used or proved; the replacement theorem honestly supplies only the pointwise Cramer certificate.

proposed.statement:
For every law in \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)\), with \(\mathcal S\) any finite binary-path support, the reshaped fixed-effect coefficient satisfies
\[
 \theta(\Pi)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{t,\ell}.
\]
For \(j,r,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), the arbitrary-path covariance kernel obeys
\[
 G_{jr}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
 -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r),
\]
\[
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
 -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\},
\]
and \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\).  If every path in \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, then \(C_{\Pi}=K_{\Pi}\), so the same two formulas hold with \(K_{\Pi}\) in place of \(C_{\Pi}\).
proposed.justification: This is the exact coefficient-by-calendar-by-causal-lag causal map on arbitrary binary-path support, with the ordered Green representation isolated as an absorbing-support corollary.
proposed.gap: The closest published RIPW result gives lag coefficients only under calendar-homogeneous effects; it does not state this arbitrary-path calendar-by-lag tensor.
proposed.consumer: The OpenTable analysis can report the precise calendar dates and causal lags contributing to each coefficient, while nonabsorbing specifications use the correct covariance kernel.

proposed.statement:
If \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\tau_{r,\ell}\) for every \(t,r\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), then \(\theta_j(\Pi)=\tau_{t,j}\) for every \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) and every legal \(t\).  For \(T=3\), \(p=1\), \(\mathcal S=\{000,001,011\}\), and \(\Pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), the calendar-varying model yields
\[
 \theta_0=(\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2,
 \qquad
 \theta_1=(-\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2+\tau_{3,1}.
\]
Thus the coefficient vector is not determined by a time-homogeneous lag-effect vector.  The first equality is coefficient algebra in the present superpopulation class, not a class-inclusion proof of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo's Theorem \(4.1\).  The published-class calendar-loading theorem supplies the faithful statistical recovery of that theorem, and the displayed witness admits an independent randomized-assignment embedding satisfying its hypotheses.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup, Assumptions 2.1--2.3, a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model, and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the corresponding average lag effect.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, a reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects, with covariance and pair-mass formulas, normalization, and exact rational diagnostics.  Under the distinct unit-indexed known-propensity conditions of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo, the corrected weighted regression with a grand intercept has the same tensor probability limit and exactly recovers their homogeneous Theorem \(4.1\).  For absorbing supports, graph connectivity gives the exact rank dimension and adjacent ratios give a pointwise Cramer sign certificate; a global classification of all sign chambers remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory establishes dynamic consistency under calendar-homogeneous effects and explicitly leaves its time-varying DATE equation beyond scope.  It permits arbitrary path support, unit-specific known propensities, and weak cross-unit dependence, so the present i.i.d. conditional-mean class is not a subclass comparison that can establish that theorem.  Existing event-study decompositions also do not provide the reshaped finite-memory calendar-by-lag tensor, an absorbing-support graph-rank law, or exact fixed-law sign certificates.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are an arbitrary-path forward loading tensor shared across two clearly separated sampling layers, plus sharp ordered diagnostics that use absorption only where it is mathematically necessary.
project_justification.fill: The project proves arbitrary-path covariance and pair-mass identities, exact normalization and rational diagnostics, a positive-law absorbing graph formula for kernel dimension, and an anchor-faithful calendar-varying probability limit for the published estimator with its grand intercept.  It also supplies a fixed-law adjacent-ratio Cramer certificate while leaving global sign-chamber enumeration open.

sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite binary-path support \(\mathcal S\) and a positive ex ante reshaping law \(\Pi\); absorption is required only for the ordered Green, graph-rank, and adjacent-ratio corollaries.
sampling_model.units: Population identification uses i.i.d. triples \((X_i,W_i,Y_i)\) from \(P\).  A separate anchor-faithful estimator theorem uses the published possibly dependent unit-indexed triangular array and its maximal-correlation condition.
sampling_model.treatment: In the base algebra, \(W_i\) may be any path in the declared finite binary support.  Ordered adoption-time results explicitly restrict that support to absorbing paths.
sampling_model.overlap: The population layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\) and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\).  The published layer instead uses known unit-specific propensities \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_*\) on the reshaping support and defines its RIPW weight to be zero off that support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a correct common generalized path propensity and pathwise conditional means.  The anchor-faithful statistical theorem is for the published known-propensity estimator; it does not assert a cross-fitted or doubly robust extension.

prose_updates.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known generalized propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence.  The new published-class theorem retains those features and the grand intercept in their equation \(4.2\), extends its probability-limit algebra to calendar-varying finite-memory effects, and recovers their Theorem \(4.1\) under homogeneity.  The separate i.i.d. conditional-mean identification class is incomparable overall and is not used as an inclusion argument.  Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients but do not study assignment-law reshaping of finite-memory lag regressors.  Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) motivate treatment-history indexing under known experimental assignment.  De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) recover time-constant random-coefficient distributed lags in complex designs.  Wright (2026) supplies adjacent public-manuscript evidence on conventional event-study diagnostics, and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) supply modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients; none supplies the present tensor and ordered support geometry.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved forward algebra covers arbitrary finite binary-path supports.  Causal identification in the superpopulation layer requires consistency, pathwise conditional mean random assignment, overlap, the stated calendar-memory conditional mean, and full rank.  The separate estimator theorem covers the published unit-indexed known-propensity setup under Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\), with a grand intercept and no i.i.d. requirement.  Absorption is used only for the Green-kernel identity, graph-rank theorem, and adjacent-ratio certificate.  The graph dimension formula requires every reshaping mass to be positive and is false at the simplex boundary without deleting zero-mass paths.  The adjacent-ratio result is pointwise; global sign-chamber classification, inverse-image optimization, closest feasible target loading, and cross-fitted doubly robust inference are not claimed here.
